statements.subject: client
statements.description: Upon receipt of a redirection response (for example, a 301 response status code), clients SHOULD use the URI(s) in the Contact header field to formulate one or more new requests based on the redirected request.
actions: formulate new requests using URIs from Contact header field

statements.subject: client
statements.description: As with proxy recursion, a client processing 3xx class responses MUST NOT add any given URI to the target set more than once.
actions: reject duplicate URI addition to target set

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the original request had a SIPS URI in the Request-URI, the client MAY choose to recurse to a non-SIPS URI, but SHOULD inform the user of the redirection to an insecure URI.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the original request had a SIPS URI in the Request-URI, the client MAY choose to recurse to a non-SIPS URI, but SHOULD inform the user of the redirection to an insecure URI.
actions: inform user of redirection to insecure URI

statements.subject: client
statements.description: As the target set grows, the client MAY generate new requests to the URIs in any order.
actions: generate new requests to URIs in target set in any order

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Requests to the URIs MAY be generated serially or in parallel.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Failures SHOULD be detected through failure response codes (codes greater than 399); for network errors the client transaction will report any transport layer failures to the transaction user.
actions: detect failure via response code greater than 399

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When a failure for a particular contact address is received, the client SHOULD try the next contact address.
actions: create new client transaction to deliver new request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: a UAC MUST copy the entire URI from the target set into the Request-URI, except for the "method-param" and "header" URI parameters (see Section 19.1.1 for a definition of these parameters).
actions: copy entire URI from target set into Request-URI
exclude method-param and header URI parameters from copy

statements.subject: message
statements.description: As a general rule, if the header field can accept a comma-separated list of values, then the new header field value MAY be appended to any existing values in the original redirected request.
actions: append new header field value to existing values in original redirected request

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If the header field does not accept multiple values, the value in the original redirected request MAY be overwritten by the header field value communicated in the contact address.
actions: overwrite header field value with value communicated in contact address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: It is RECOMMENDED that the UAC reuse the same To, From, and Call-ID used in the original redirected request, but the UAC MAY also choose to update the Call-ID header field value for new requests, for example.
actions: reuse To header from original redirected request
reuse From header from original redirected request
reuse Call-ID from original redirected request

statements.subject: client
statements.description: It is RECOMMENDED that the UAC reuse the same To, From, and Call-ID used in the original redirected request, but the UAC MAY also choose to update the Call-ID header field value for new requests, for example.
actions: update Call-ID header field value for new request

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Finally, once the new request has been constructed, it is sent using a new client transaction, and therefore MUST have a new branch ID in the top Via field as discussed in Section 8.1.1.7.
actions: assign new branch ID to top Via field of new request

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In all other respects, requests sent upon receipt of a redirect response SHOULD re-use the header fields and bodies of the original request.
actions: re-use header fields and bodies from original request in new request
